title: Twelve Facades, One Sky
paragraph: The sky never changed. Twelve times I stood square to a building, waited for the traffic to clear, and let the same flat grey light fall across a different wall of concrete. Set side by side they stop being buildings and become a family — siblings photographed against the one backdrop that refuses to have a mood.

title: The Building That Stares Back
paragraph: Perfect symmetry is unsettling. Stand in front of this one and it seems to notice you — every window matched, every fin doubled, the entrance a mouth held exactly in the middle. I framed it the way it wanted to be framed and stepped back.

title: Nine to Five in Béton Brut
paragraph: A government block on a Tuesday morning: nothing happens on the outside, everything is implied within. The concrete is honest about what it is — a filing cabinet the size of a city street, catalogued here in the plainest light I could find.

title: Helix in Shadow
paragraph: A parking ramp is a staircase that forgot it was for cars. Looking up the core, the spiral tightens into itself, each turn darker than the last, until the top is just a suggestion of daylight swallowed by the coil.

title: Fire Escape Fugue
paragraph: Zigzag, landing, zigzag, landing — a stair is a rhythm bolted to a wall. I waited for the sun to cut it into hard diagonals and shot the repetition until it started to sound like something.

title: Laundry Day on the Fourteenth Floor
paragraph: The grid wants to be perfect and the tenants won't let it. Two hundred identical balconies, and on one of them a line of washing flags in the wind — the single human hand that breaks the architect's arithmetic.

title: Three Hundred Windows, One Light On
paragraph: At dusk the tower turns into a spreadsheet of dark cells. Then, near the top, one window glows — someone home, someone awake — and the whole anonymous slab suddenly has an address.

title: The Grain of the Formwork
paragraph: Before it was concrete it was wood. The planks that shaped the pour left their grain pressed into the surface — a fossil of the mould, timber remembered in stone. Up close the wall stops being a wall.

title: Where the Water Ran
paragraph: Rain writes on concrete. Years of it, running the same paths down the same face, leave stains that no architect drew — dark rivers of weathering that turn a flat panel into a map of its own history.

title: Vertigo, Upward
paragraph: Lie on your back at the base of a tower and the walls fall inward. Parallel lines, told they should meet, obey — rushing up toward a point in a sky wiped clean of everything but light.

title: The Sky Is a Triangle
paragraph: Between two buildings, the sky gets rationed. Stand in the gap, look up, and what's left of the heavens is a hard-edged sliver — a geometric offcut the architecture forgot to claim.

title: Lobby Light at 2 A.M.
paragraph: After midnight the building goes black except for one warm rectangle at street level — the lobby, lit for no one, glowing inside the dark concrete mass like a coal that won't go out.

title: Floodlit and Alone
paragraph: The floodlights come on and the plaza empties. Concrete that looked heavy by day turns theatrical at night — a stage set with no actors, lit hard from below, holding its pose for the long exposure.

title: A Pastel Shelter on the Steppe
paragraph: Out where the road runs straight to the horizon, someone once poured a small monument to waiting. Faded mint and dusty coral against a grey sky — a concrete bus stop still standing for a bus that comes twice a day, if at all.

title: Twelve Bus Stops on the Old Highway
paragraph: No two are alike. Whoever built these was bored of the brief and turned every shelter into a small argument — a wing, a wave, a concrete flower — scattered along a highway that has mostly forgotten them.
